title.en: Bathsheba Before the Throne: Solomon Anointed in a Hurry
title.zh: 拔示巴進御前：所羅門急立為王

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Adonijah exalts himself at the stone of Zoheleth while the aged king 'knew not' his bed. Nathan directs Bathsheba to remind David of his oath, then himself enters; David has Solomon ride the king's mule to Gihon, be anointed by Zadok, and the shofar is blown — 'the city was in an uproar'. Adonijah's feast dissolves in fear; Solomon's first act of clemency spares him.
summary.zh: 亞多尼雅在隱羅結旁自高，而老王「不知」床事。拿單教拔示巴提起大衛的誓言，自己隨後進見；大衛命所羅門騎王的騾子下基訓，由撒督膏立，吹角——「城裡的眾民都大聲吹角」。亞多尼雅的宴席聞風潰散；所羅門首行寬仁，存其性命。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil out of the Tent, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the horn; and all the people said: 'Long live king Solomon.' And all the people came up after him, and the people piped with pipes, and rejoiced with great joy, so that the earth rent with the sound of them.

title.en: Give Thy Servant a Listening Heart

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: At Gibeon Solomon offers a thousand burnt-offerings, and the LORD appears to him by night: 'Ask what I shall give thee.' The king asks 'an understanding heart to judge Thy people, that I may discern between good and evil' — no long life, no riches. 'Because thou hast asked this thing... behold, I have done according to thy word' — plus riches and honour thrown in, 'so that there hath not been any among the kings like unto thee'.
summary.zh: 在基遍獻一千燔祭，夜間耶和華向所羅門顯現：「你願我賜你什麼，你可以求。」王求「能分辨是非的心判斷你的民」——不求壽，不求富。「你所求的我已賜給你」——並加富足尊榮，「列王中沒有一個能比你的」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Give Thy servant therefore an understanding heart to judge Thy people, that I may discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this Thy so great a people? And the speech pleased the LORD, that Solomon had asked this thing. ... Behold, I have given thee a wise and a discerning heart; so that there hath been none like thee before thee, neither shall any arise like unto thee.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 3:9, 12 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: Divide the Living Child: The Judgment of Solomon
title.zh: 將活孩子劈成兩半：所羅門的判斷

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Two harlots both claim one surviving child. Solomon orders a sword — 'Divide the living child in two, and give half unto the one, and half unto the other'. The true mother surrenders her claim — 'give her the child... but don't kill it'; the false consents. 'And all Israel heard of the judgment... and they feared the king; for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him.'
summary.zh: 兩妓女爭一活子。所羅門命取刀——「將活孩子劈成兩半，一半給這婦人，一半給那婦人」。真母捨子——「將孩子給她吧，萬不可殺他」；假母同意。「以色列眾人聽見王這樣判斷，就都敬畏他，因為見他心裡有神的智慧。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then spake the woman whose the living child was unto the king, for her bowels yearned upon her son, and she said: 'O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it.' But the other said: 'Let it be neither mine nor thine; divide it.' Then the king answered and said: 'Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof.'

title.en: Will God Indeed Dwell on the Earth? Temple Dedication
title.zh: 神果真住在地上嗎？聖殿奉獻

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The elders, the ark with cherubim-shadowing poles, and the glory-cloud fill the house 'so that the priests could not stand to minister'. Solomon's prayer asks heaven's scandal: 'Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee; how much less this house that I have builded!' — a house for the Name, for prayer toward it in every calamity, for the stranger who comes from a far country.
summary.zh: 長老、有基路伯蔭影的約櫃與榮光之雲充滿殿，「甚至祭司不能站立供職」。所羅門的禱告直指天之悖論：「天和天上的天尚且不足你居住的，何況我所建的這殿呢！」——為名的殿，為各樣災殃中向殿的祈禱，也為從遠方來的外邦人。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Read as Sukkot haftarah; the dedication prayer structures later Jewish liturgy of petition.

passages.text: But will God in very truth dwell on the earth? Behold, heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee; how much less this house that I have builded! Yet have Thou respect unto the prayer of Thy servant, and to his supplication, O LORD my God, to hearken unto the cry and to the prayer which Thy servant prayeth before Thee this day; that Thine eyes may be open toward this house night and day.

title.en: The Queen of Sheba Comes with Hard Questions

region.en: Jerusalem (visiting queen from Sheba, South Arabia)
region.zh: 耶路撒冷（示巴南方來訪女王）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Sheba's queen, 'hearing of the fame of Solomon', comes with camels bearing spices, gold, and precious stones, and with hard questions. Everything she sees — the house, the food, the apparel, the burnt-offering — 'there was no more spirit in her': 'It was a true report... the half was not told me.' Gold and spices change hands, and no more spice came 'such as the queen of Sheba gave' until her day's end.
summary.zh: 示巴女王「聽見所羅門的名聲」，攜駱駝馱香料、金子、寶石與難題而來。凡她所見——宮室、飲食、衣服、燔祭——「就詫異得神不守舍」：「我先前的話是真的……我所聽見的，不及一半。」金與香料交易，示巴女王所給的香料「以後再沒有這樣的香料」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Ethiopian tradition identifies her dynasty with Makeda (cross-ref Ethiopian records, not yet present).

passages.text: And when the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, and the house that he had built, and the food of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel... there was no more spirit in her. And she said to the king: 'It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thine acts, and of thy wisdom. Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it; and, behold, the half was not told me.'

title.en: Jeroboam's Calves: The Kingdom Divided
title.zh: 耶羅波安的金牛：國分裂

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The prophet Ahijah tears his new cloak into twelve pieces and gives ten to Jeroboam: 'behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon'. After Rehoboam's tyranny ('my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions'), the ten tribes secede. Fearful of Jerusalem's temple, Jeroboam sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan: 'behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt' — the sin the Book of Kings keeps repeating.
summary.zh: 先知亞希雅將新衣撕成十二片，予耶羅波安十片：「看哪，我必將國從所羅門手裡奪回」。羅波安暴政（「我父親用鞭子責打你們，我要用蠍子鞭責打你們」）之後，十支派分離。懼聖殿朝聖，耶羅波安在伯特利與但立金牛犢：「以色列人哪，你們上耶路撒冷去實在難；看哪，這是領你們出埃及地的神。」——列王記不斷重複的罪。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Ahijah laid hold of the new garment that was on him, and rent it in twelve pieces. And he said to Jeroboam: 'Take thee ten pieces; for thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel: Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee.'

Rehoboam's arrogance split the united monarchy at Shechem; the people's cry, 'What portion have we in David?', sent the northern tribes home. Jeroboam fortified Shechem, then, fearing pilgrimage would rebind hearts to Jerusalem, cast two calves and installed non-Levitical priests, kept a festival 'in the month which he had devised of his own heart' — and the deuteronomistic verdict — 'this thing became a sin' — follows every northern king's obituary. Paraphrase of 1 Kings 12:1-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Man of God from Judah and the Lion on the Road

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: A 'man of God out of Judah' cries against Jeroboam's altar — 'O altar, altar, thus saith the LORD: Behold, a son shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name' — and the altar cracks. Offered a reward, he refuses food or water: 'so was it charged me by the word of the LORD'. An old prophet lies to him, a lion kills him on the road 'but did not eat the ass', and the old prophet buries him: 'the words which he cried... shall surely come to pass.'
summary.zh: 猶大的神人在耶羅波安的壇前呼叫——「壇哪，壇哪！耶和華如此說：大衛家裡必生一個兒子，名叫約西亞」——壇即裂開。受款待而不受：「我奉耶和華的命令，不可喫飯喝水」。老先知以謊言留他，路上獅子咬死他「卻沒有喫驢」，老先知葬之：「他奉耶和華的命指著伯特利壇說的話必定應驗。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And behold, a lion met him by the way, and slew him; and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it; the lion also stood by the carcase. And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase; and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

title.en: The Vineyard of Naboth and the Blood of Jezebel
title.zh: 拿伯的葡萄園與耶洗別的血

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Ahab covets Naboth's ancestral vineyard beside his palace; Naboth refuses — 'The LORD forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee'. Jezebel's forged letters stage a fast and false blasphemy charges; Naboth is stoned, and Ahab takes the field. Elijah meets him: 'Hast thou killed, and also taken possession?... In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.'
summary.zh: 亞哈貪戀王宮旁拿伯的祖業葡萄園；拿伯拒之：「我敬畏耶和華，萬不敢將我先人留下的產業給你。」耶洗別偽造書信設禁食與假瀆神之罪；拿伯被石擊，亞哈得田。以利亞迎之：「你殺了人，又得他的產業麼？……狗在何處舔拿伯的血，也必在何處舔你的血。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Naboth's ancestral inheritance frames Israelite land law.

passages.text: And Ahab said unto Elijah: 'Hast thou found me, O mine enemy?' And he answered: 'I have found thee; because thou hast sold thyself to do that which is evil in the sight of the LORD. Behold, I will bring evil upon thee, and will utterly sweep away after thee; and will make thine house like the house of Jeroboam... because thou hast provoked Me to anger, and hast made Israel to sin.'

title.en: Ravens Feed Elijah by the Brook Cherith
title.zh: 烏鴉在基立溪旁供養以利亞

region.en: Brook Cherith, east of the Jordan

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The Tishbite announces to Ahab: 'As the LORD... liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word'. God sends him to the brook Cherith to drink of the stream — 'and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there' — and the ravens bring him bread and flesh morning and evening until the brook dries up.
summary.zh: 提斯比人向亞哈宣告：「我指著所事奉永生耶和華以色列的神起誓，這幾年我若不禱告，必不降露不下雨。」神遣他往基立溪喝水——「我已吩咐烏鴉在那裡供養你」——烏鴉早晚給他餅與肉，直至溪水乾涸。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook. And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.

title.en: The Widow's Handful of Meal at Zarephath

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Sent to a foreign widow gathering sticks, Elijah asks a morsel; she has only 'a handful of meal in the barrel, and a little oil in the cruse' — enough for one last cake before death. 'Fear not... for thus saith the LORD: The barrel of meal shall not waste.' The jar and cruse never empty. When her son dies, the prophet carries him upstairs and prays three times — 'O LORD my God, let the child's soul come back into his body' — and he revives.
summary.zh: 遣至外邦撿柴寡婦旁，以利亞求一點餅；她只有「罈內的一把麵，瓶裡的一點油」——最後一餐。 「不要懼怕……耶和華如此說：罈內的麵必不減少。」罈與瓶永不空。兒子死時，先知抱他上樓三次禱告——「求你使這孩子的魂仍入他的身體」——孩子復活。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Elijah stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the LORD, and said: 'O LORD my God, I pray Thee, let this child's soul come back into his body.' And the LORD hearkened unto the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came back into his body, and he revived. ... And the woman said to Elijah: 'Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the LORD in thy mouth is truth.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 1 Kings 17:21-24 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: The God That Answereth by Fire: Carmel

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: On Carmel Elijah challenges 450 prophets of Baal: 'call ye on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the LORD'. They dance and cut themselves till evening; there is 'no voice, nor any that answered'. Elijah repairs the broken altar, drenches the sacrifice three times, and prays — fire falls, consumes wood, stones, dust, and water. 'And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces; and they said: The LORD, He is the God; the LORD, He is the God.'
summary.zh: 在迦密山以利亞挑戰四百五十巴力先知：「求告你們神的名，我也求告耶和華的名」。他們跳舞自割直到傍晚，「沒有聲音，沒有應允的」。以利亞重修毀壞的壇，三次澆透祭牲禱告——火降，燒盡燔祭、木柴、石頭、塵土與水。「眾民看見了，就俯伏在地，說：耶和華是神！耶和華是神！」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then the fire of the LORD fell, and consumed the burnt-offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench. And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces; and they said: 'The LORD, He is the God; the LORD, He is the God.'

Elijah's taunt became proverbial: 'cry aloud; for he is a god; either he is meditating, or gone aside, or on a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth'. After the fire, the prophets of Baal are seized at the brook Kishon, rain returns — 'there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man's hand' — and Elijah girds up his loins and runs before Ahab's chariot to Jezreel. Paraphrase of 1 Kings 18:27, 40-46 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: The Still Small Voice of Horeb

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Jezebel's threat sends Elijah a day's journey into the wilderness to lie under a juniper tree and ask to die. An angel touches him twice with cake and water — 'the journey is too great for thee' — and he goes to Horeb, where wind, earthquake, and fire each pass 'but the LORD was not in them', until 'a still small voice'. God sends him back: anoint Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha; seven thousand have not bowed to Baal.
summary.zh: 耶洗別的恐嚇使以利亞逃入曠野一日，躺在一棵羅騰樹下求死。天使兩次以餅水觸之——「這路太遠，你不能走」——他到何烈山；狂風、地震、烈火各有其至，「耶和華卻不在其中」，直至「微小的聲音」。神遣他回去：膏哈薛、耶戶、以利沙；還有七千人未曾向巴力屈膝。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And, behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and broke in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind; and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake; and after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire; and after the fire a still small voice.

title.en: Fire from Heaven: Ahaziah's Two Captains of Fifty
title.zh: 天降之火：亞哈謝兩個五十夫長

region.zh: 撒瑪利亞山頂（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Sick Ahaziah sends messengers to consult Baal-zebub, god of Ekron; Elijah intercepts them: 'Is it because there is no God in Israel?' A captain of fifty with his men, sent to fetch the prophet, calls him 'thou man of God' and is consumed by fire from heaven; the second suffers likewise. The third captain falls on his knees — 'let my life, and the life of these fifty, be precious in thy sight' — and Elijah goes down to pronounce the king's death.
summary.zh: 患病的亞哈謝遣使求問以革倫的巴力西卜；以利亞攔阻：「以色列中豈沒有神麼？」五十夫長稱其「神人」而被天火燒滅；第二隊同然。第三個俯伏——「願我的性命與這五十個人的性命在你眼前看為寶貴」——以利亞乃下去宣告王之死。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Elijah answered and said to the captain of fifty: 'If I be a man of God, let fire come down from heaven, and consume thee and thy fifty.' And there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, 2 Kings 1:10 (public domain). The narrative repeats for the second captain and contrasts the third captain's humility.

title.en: The Chariot of Fire: Elijah Taken Up

region.zh: 過約旦河往耶利哥（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Elisha, warned thrice, refuses to leave his master: 'as the LORD liveth... I will not leave thee'. Fifty prophets watch from afar as Elijah smites the Jordan with his rolled mantle and the waters divide. He asks his parting gift; Elisha dares: 'a double portion of thy spirit'. 'A chariot of fire, and horses of fire, appeared... and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.' The mantle falls; Elisha smites the waters — 'and they parted hither and thither; and he went over.'
summary.zh: 以利沙三得警告而不離：「我指著永生的耶和華……起誓，我必不離開你」。五十先知遠觀以利亞捲起外衣打水，水就分開。臨別求恩賜；以利沙敢求：「願感動你的靈加倍的感動我。」「有火車火馬出現……以利亞乘旋風升天去了。」外衣掉下；以利沙打水——「水也左右分開了」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Elijah's non-death seeds the Seder-cup expectation and Malachi's 'returning Elijah' (Mal 3:23).

passages.text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, which parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven. And Elisha saw it, and he cried: 'My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and the horsemen thereof!' And he saw him no more.

title.en: The Widow's Oil That Would Not Stop

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: A widow of the prophets' guild, debt-ridden with creditors coming for her two sons, owns one jar of oil. Elisha commands: borrow empty vessels, 'borrow not a few', and pour indoors. She pours until every vessel is full — 'and the oil stayed'. Sold, the oil pays the debt and the family lives 'of the rest'.
summary.zh: 先知門徒的遺孀債台高築，債主來取二子為奴，家中只有一瓶油。以利沙命：借空器皿，「不要少借」，關門倒油。她倒至一切器皿都滿了——「油就止住了」。賣油還債，母子「靠所剩的度日」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And when they were full, she said unto her son: 'Bring me yet a vessel.' And he said unto her: 'There is not a vessel more.' And the oil stayed. Then she came and told the man of God. And he said: 'Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.'

title.en: The Shunammite's Room and Her Son Twice Given
title.zh: 書念婦人的小樓與兩次得子

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: A great woman of Shunem builds the prophet a small furnished room; offered recompense, she asks nothing — 'I dwell among mine own people'. Elisha promises her a son 'at this season next year', and the child is born. Years later he dies of sunstroke in the harvest field; she lays him on the prophet's bed, rides to Carmel, grips Elisha's feet, and refuses release until the prophet raises the boy — sneeze after sneeze — alive.
summary.zh: 書念的大婦人為先知蓋小樓，陳設床榻桌椅燈；蒙報以恩而不求——「我在本民中安然居住」。以利沙許以明年此時得一子，果然。多年後孩子在田間中暑而死；她將他放在先知的床上，騎驢上迦密山，抓住神人以利沙的腳，不放直到先知使孩子復活——連連打了七個噴嚏。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And when Elisha was come into the house, behold, the child was dead, and laid upon his bed. And he went in therefore, and shut the door upon them twain, and prayed unto the LORD. And he went up, and lay upon the child, and put his mouth upon his mouth, and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands; and he stretched himself upon him; and the flesh of the child waxed warm.

title.en: Naaman Washes Seven Times in the Jordan
title.zh: 乃縵在約旦河沐浴七次

region.zh: 撒瑪利亞附近的約旦河

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The Syrian captain, 'a great man... but a leper', hears from an Israelite captive girl of 'the prophet that is in Samaria'. Elisha sends only a messenger — 'go and wash in the Jordan seven times' — and Naaman storms off: 'Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?' His servants' gentle logic prevails; he dips seven times, 'and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.' He takes two mule-loads of Israel's earth home to worship the LORD.
summary.zh: 敘利亞元帥「為尊為大……卻長了大痲瘋」，從以色列擄來的小女子口中得知「撒瑪利亞的先知」。以利沙只遣使者——「去在約旦河中沐浴七回」——乃縵怒而去：「大馬士革的河亞罷拿與法珥法豈不比以色列的一切水更好麼？」僕人婉勸；七次沐浴，「他的肉復原，好像小孩子的肉，就潔淨了」。他馱兩騾子以色列土回國，好獻祭與耶和華。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean. And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him; and he said: 'Behold now, I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel.'

title.en: Horses and Chariots of Fire at Dothan

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 9th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Elisha keeps foretelling the king of Israel every move of the Syrian army. Surrounded by horses and chariots at Dothan, his servant panics — and the prophet prays: 'open his eyes, that he may see. And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw; and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.' The army is smitten with blindness and led to Samaria, where Elisha forbids slaughter: 'Set bread and water before them... and they went to their master.'
summary.zh: 以利沙頻將敘利亞軍的行動預告以色列王。在多坍被馬兵戰車四面圍困，僕人驚惶——先知禱告：「求你開他的眼目，使他能看見。耶和華開他的眼目，他就看見滿山有火車火馬圍繞以利沙。」敘軍眼目昏迷，被引至撒瑪利亞；以利沙禁止殺戮：「擺設飯，給他們喫了喝……他們就回到主人那裡去了。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Elisha prayed, and said: 'LORD, I pray Thee, open his eyes, that he may see.' And the LORD opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw; and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha. And as they came down to him, Elisha prayed unto the LORD, and said: 'Smite this people, I pray Thee, with blindness.' And He smote them with blindness according to the word of Elisha.

title.en: The Angel in the Camp: Jerusalem against Sennacherib
title.zh: 營中的天使：耶路撒冷對西拿基立

region.zh: 耶路撒冷城牆；亞述營地

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The Rabshakeh taunts Jerusalem in Judean from the wall: 'Hath any of the gods of the nations ever delivered his land?' Hezekiah spreads the letter before the LORD in the Temple and prays: 'save us... that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that Thou art the LORD God, even Thou only'. Isaiah's oracle answers; that night 'the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand', and Sennacherib returns to Nineveh, later slain in the house of Nisroch.
summary.zh: 拉伯沙基在牆外用猶大語譏誚：「列國的神有哪一個救他本國脫離亞述王的手呢？」希西家將書信在殿裡展開在耶和華面前禱告：「求你救我們脫離亞述王的手，使天下萬國都知道惟獨你耶和華是神」。以賽亞的諭言回應；當夜「耶和華的使者出去，在亞述營中殺了十八萬五千人」，西拿基立拔營回尼尼微，後在尼斯洛廟裡被殺。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Parallel reliefs (Taylor Prism) preserve the Assyrian version of the siege.

passages.text: And it came to pass that night, that the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand; and when men arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses. So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt in Nineveh.

title.en: The Book Found in the House of the LORD

texts.period: Narrative set 622 BCE; composed c. 7th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: During Temple repairs under the boy-king Josiah, Hilkiah the priest finds 'a book of the law of the LORD'. The scribe Shaphan reads it to the king, who rends his clothes: 'great is the wrath of the LORD that is kindled against us'. Huldah the prophetess confirms the doom — 'but because thine heart was tender' Josiah dies in peace. Then comes the great purge: idols burned, the high places defiled, Passover kept 'as it is written in the book of this covenant... from the days of the judges', none like it since.
summary.zh: 少年王約西亞修殿時，大祭司希勒家尋得「律法書」。書記沙番讀與王聽，王撕裂衣服：「耶和華向我們大發烈怒」。女先知戶勒大確認災禍——「但因你心裡柔軟」約西亞平安而終。隨後大清除：偶像焚燒、邱壇污穢、照「書上所寫的約」守逾越節——「自從士師……沒有守過這樣的逾越節」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Josiah's reform is a anchor-point for biblical scholarship on Deuteronomy's composition.

passages.text: And it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the book of the law, that he rent his clothes. And the king commanded... saying: 'Inquire ye of the LORD for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found; for great is the wrath of the LORD that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not hearkened unto the words of this book, to do according unto all that which is written concerning us.'

title.en: The Burning of the House of the LORD

texts.period: Narrative set 587/586 BCE; composed c. 6th-5th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah the city wall is breached; the king's sons are slain before his eyes, his eyes put out, and he is carried to Babylon in fetters. The Temple, palace, and every great house are burned; the walls are broken down; the vessels of the house of the LORD are cut in pieces and carried off. Gedaliah is set over the remnant and assassinated — and the people, fearing the Chaldeans, go down into Egypt. 'So Judah was carried away captive out of his land.'
summary.zh: 西底家十一年，城被攻破；王眾子在他眼前被殺，他的眼被剜，帶鎖鍊被擄到巴比倫。耶和華的殿、王宮、大宅盡焚；城牆拆毀；聖殿的器皿被切成銅塊擄去。基大利被立管餘民而被殺——眾人懼迦勒底人，下埃及去。「這樣，猶大人被擄離開本地。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The exilic trauma structures Jewish historical memory (Tisha B'Av).

passages.text: And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month... Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came unto Jerusalem. And he burnt the house of the LORD, and the king's house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every great man's house, burnt he with fire. And all the army of the Chaldeans, that were with the captain of the guard, broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about.
